correctness.rationale: For fixed prime-power q>=2 and all n>=1, selecting rank-r A and rank-s B into ker(A) gives N(n;r,s)=[n r]_q^2 |GL_r| [n-r s]_q[n s]_q|GL_s| when r+s<=n, including r=0,s=0 boundaries. Summing B first gives W_n(r)=q^(n^2+r(n-r)) Q_n^2/[Q_r Q_(n-r)^2]. Center r=m+j at n=2m+epsilon. A bounded q^(-j^2+epsilon*j) envelope proves the parity-sensitive theta normalization and total-variation R-m law. Conditional rectangular B has full-row-rank probability Q_n/Q_r; a union bound gives sharp first homology defect with coefficient Theta_(1-epsilon)/[(q-1)Theta_epsilon] and a 2-dimensional annihilator union bound gives P(H>=2)=O_q(q^(-2m)). This reconstructs the universal fixed-field proof rather than extrapolating finite counts.

value.rationale: The zero-product incidence relation is intrinsic to finite matrix monoids; the rank is their natural Green-stratum invariant and homology is a canonical invariant of the resulting short complex. Global pair-uniform conditioning biases both ranks toward n/2, unlike sequentially uniform chain-complex models; the explicit discrete-Gaussian limit and exponentially rare nonexactness quantify the bias. The sharp tail coefficient is an independently useful natural asymptotic fact, not a small arbitrary computation.
